label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8) whose first tokens are from {a,b,p,o,k,j,u,m,v,3}
explanation: Almost exclusively a delimiter-step unit: 98% of activation mass is at the <DEL> input (t == L, the step that outputs original token 0); it essentially never fires in the original phase or later copy steps (small leakage at the last original token and at recall_idx 1). Within <DEL> steps it fires on only 12% of sequences, gated mainly by length: rate rises steeply with L (L=9 about 37%, L=8 about 24%, L<=6 near zero), and L>=8 carries about 85% of the mass. Beyond length, it prefers sequences whose first token (the token about to be output) is one of a, p, o, k, b, j, u, 3, m, or whose second token is one of b, a, v, m, k, j, p, u; these give 4-5x lift. Magnitude grows with L and with these first-token identities (top activations are all L=8-9 sequences starting with a, b, p, j, k, o, 3). The token preference is graded and distributed rather than a crisp set, so precision tops out near 0.5: phase==1 & L>=7 alone recovers 95% of mass at 23% precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: p, a, o, k; copy phase: a, v, m, b; input phase: ) and the next token to output (most: b, v, a, m, k, p; least: 0, -, z, x); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, t=8, t=9.
